en: The Ritual Manual for the Yoga Recitation of the Great Wrathful and Swift Kumāra Vajra, the Transformation Body of the Buddha Amitāyus,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India by Imperial Decree.
Now, following the Yoga system as taught in the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*,
regarding the ritual for recitation in the western direction of the Blazing Vajra Family:
if there are practitioners who cultivate this, they should receive it upon their heads in accordance with these instructions.
Having first received empowerment from the ācārya, one should next select a pure location:
by a river, a stream, a spring, or a mountain peak;
in an araṇya, or at a place where sages have attained the Way.
Whether in a monastic dwelling, pure and grandly adorned,
or in whatever place one finds delight, one who desires to practice the methods for *siddhi* should receive and uphold them with diligent effort within the various Vajra families.
This Dharma is most profound and subtle; through the power of mantra-consecration, one subdues and wins over others.
By visualizing all the Buddhas and contemplating the *iṣṭadevatā*, the power of mantra is peerless.
He who can crush great obstacles—merely by holding his mantra-syllables, transformation-buddhas emerge from his mouth;
all manner of auspicious matters arrive of their own accord as soon as they are thought of. Homage to Amitāyus!
May I, through the power of these merits, swiftly attain the siddhi of transcendence;
having made this vast and solemn vow, one should next pay homage to all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas,
and confess the transgressions of the three karmas.
From past lives, I have wandered through birth and death;
now, before the Great Holy One, I repent with all my heart.
Just as the Buddhas of the past repented, so do I now.
The practitioner should next pay homage to all the assemblies of noble ones with a single prostration to the secret mantra.
This accumulation of gathered wisdom and prostrations is like the turning of all the sūtras; it eliminates doubt and brings about certainty.
Next, form the seal for opening the gate: With both hands in vajra-fists, raise the seal while uttering the sound *HŪṂ*.
Having touched the gate and awakened it, one is able to subdue inner and outer māras. The mantra is as follows:

Kumārakrodha holds the water-seal: first, with the hands of meditative equipoise (samādhi-mudrā) extended flat, the dhyāna-finger presses upon the patience-finger as armor. Reciting the secret mantra seven times, one takes hold of a willow branch;
[one should contemplate] the space between the interior and exterior of one's own body.
To purify and remove the stains of afflictions, the mantra for sprinkling purification is as follows:

*Buddha-kula:* Half-opened petals, with *vīrya* (diligence), *vīrya* at the end, supported by *kṣānti* (patience), *praṇidhāna* (vow), *dhyāna* (meditation), and *prajñā* (wisdom). One should visualize the Tathāgata in one's mind.
The mantra is as follows:
The Lotus Samādhi Seal—extending the ten fingers and slightly bending the thumbs and wisdom-fingers, join the middle and ring fingers;
with single-minded concentration, one should perform the visualization.
The Eight-Petaled Avalokiteśvara: The secret mantra is as follows.
Next, bind the Vajra Family mudrā: with the two hands turned back-to-back, hook the *jñāna* and *tarjanī* fingers against the *dhyāna* and *vajra* fingers. Visualize holding a vajra in the mind.

For the protection of the body: cross the hands within; raise the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers like banners, and attach the *vīrya* and *bala* fingers like hooks. Press the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers over the *śīla* fingers;
thus the seal is formed at the five locations as armor. The Mantra: [Mantra follows]
Next is the Earth Element Seal (*pṛthivī-mudrā*): With the patience and precept fingers encircling the directions, place the vow fingers into the palms;

join the meditation and wisdom fingers together, and touch the earth with both the generosity, skillful means, diligence, and meditation fingers, as well as the wisdom fingers. The mantra is as follows:
The Vajra Wall of the Quarters: With the previous mudrā, open the *citta* (wisdom) and *jñāna* (meditation) fingers and extend them sideways like the shape of a wall. The mantra is as follows.
Next, one should invite the tutelary deity, with the *samādhi* and *prajñā* [fingers] interlaced within.
Joining the wrists at the middle joints, extend the *jñāna-muṣṭi* (wisdom fist) upward to perform the invocation and the expulsion of obstacles;

with the right *prajñā-muṣṭi* (wisdom fist) pressing the *jñāna-pāramitā*, form a three-pronged *viśvavajra* (crossed vajra) at the waist; the *samādhi-muṣṭi* (concentration fist) rotates above the crown of the head.
The mantra for forming the boundary on the left and right is as follows:

The net-seal is performed according to the previous wall-seal; with the wisdom-finger (middle finger) and the dhyāna-finger (ring finger) held at the base of the forefinger, rotate three times over the top to form the net above.
The fire court is sealed by wisdom; erect the *dhyāna* and *jñāna* mudrās, circling them three times to the right to form a fierce flame. The mantra is as follows.
Next, bind the flower-offering seat: with both hands, form the shape of a lotus.
The mantra for slightly bending [the fingers] to open the eight petals is:
Oṃ vajramālya svāhā. The mantra for offering the arghya water is:

For the offering of scented ointment, extend the palms in the mudrā of meditative concentration; for the flower, hold the right wrist with the wisdom hand, with fingers interlaced and facing upward; for the incense, join the two wind fingers, attach them to the two space fingers, and raise them back-to-back;
for the lamp, attach the dhyāna and wisdom fingers to the advancing power fingers.

Offering food, look up and join [the hands]. Slightly bending the fire and wind wheels (the middle and ring fingers), attach the two thumbs to the side of the wind [fingers]. The mantra is as follows:
Form the lamp mudrā into a fist; extend the patience finger (middle finger) and the meditation finger (ring finger) to pinch [the thumb].
The mantra for universally making offerings to the expanse of space and placing the vajra-palm upon the crown while mentally pervading the entire dharma-realm is as follows:
Next, with a pure and elegant voice, offer praise to the Holy Lord.
Next, bind the uṣṇīṣa mudrā: with fists clenched, extend the forefinger and middle finger to touch at the crown, remaining seated without wavering.
In meditative equipoise (*samādhi*), visualize within the lotus of one’s own heart a sun disc of blazing majesty.
The syllable HŪṂ forms a single-pronged [vajra], which transforms into the Wrathful Lord;
his right leg is straight and his left slightly bent as he tramples upon a blue lotus.
His body is the color of yellow clouds, and his hair is red, standing straight up.
Adorned with jeweled necklaces upon his body, draped with tiger skin across his shoulders;
raising the wisdom-hand high while holding the vajra, and extending the hand of fearlessness downward;
he crushes the armies of the devas and māras, possessing incomparable power of supernatural faculties.
When the mantra syllables were first spoken, auspicious clouds of five colors appeared;
emanated Buddhas filled the void of space. The devas came to scatter flowers, as did the gandharvas, kinnaras, and the twenty-eight classes of beings.
And all other great seers, with palms joined in reverence, pay homage;
Visualizing clearly with an undistracted mind, one forms the Great Anusārinī Vidyārājñī mudrā of the Vajrakumāra: The Wisdom Hand forms an empty fist.
The *bha* syllable is at the back of the vow; the power-syllable (*bala*) points toward the direction, while the skillful means (*upāya*) syllable points toward the back.
The wisdom (*jñāna*) syllable likewise presses upon the insight (*prajñā*).
With the index fingers raised like banners, through this empowerment, [the rite is accomplished].
The mantra that can encompass sovereign power, the unsurpassed phrase of wrathful mind and secret mudrā:
Join the two palms in the void, interlace the water fingers,
insert them into the tiger’s mouth, and hook the wind fingers downward toward the space.
The earth-wheel is held upright like a tusk; with a heart of true great compassion, one delivers others from the sufferings of the three miserable realms.
One quickly attains *siddhi* and then performs the seal that destroys inauspiciousness: crossing the inner earth and water wheels.
The fire element bends back the shell; wind and space form the vertical mudrā.
Whether walking or resting, by maintaining the mind and binding the thought, calamities, obstacles, and evil dreams are extinguished.
Next, the supernormal powers are employed interchangeably.
From the previous mudrā, open the two winds;
this is the gate of mastery for accomplishing the Vajra Dharma-penetration.
For the Lord Deity’s *Ran-lu* seal, cross the outer fingers of the earth-wheels and hook the two wind-wheels together.
The fire and water [mudrās] are joined vertically; with the two space [mudrās] holding the fire peaks,
by merely performing this consecration, clouds of divine music and offerings are accomplished according to one's will as true reality, subduing all demons through the wrathful samādhi.
The water element gives rise to fire and wind;
the fire and wind curl into a fist while earth and space are held upright and raised.
Through this secret seal of majestic power, one crushes the fierce fangs of wild beasts; no enemy demons can withstand it.
Next, bind the seal of the Kings of Records: following the previous procedure for the chaotic records, join the two empty fingers and press the root of the water-finger.
This shall employ the Four Great Kings, powerful benevolent deities, and others to shake the great trichiliocosm.
The Vajra King’s Body Protection: With the fire [finger] bent, the right empty [finger] presses down upon the water [finger], which is held at the wheel of space;
with the earth [finger] on the back of the water [finger], one invites the Vajra to cause the body to attain firmness.
Without being corrupted by the three realms, one can protect the practitioner;
To cure the diseases of body and mind, The vajra-fists of concentration and wisdom join the wind-wheels at the crown,
With the two voids placed at the side of fire.
Recite the mantra seven times while visualizing a wrathful mind;
when spirits and ghosts create obstacles, they shall be subdued and dispersed.
This is the Vajra-Harṣa-mudrā (Vajra Joy Mudrā): form a hollow-fisted fist with the right hand.
Emptying the hands, pressing the water, and turning the back of the wind;
extending the *mudrā* of generosity and patience, one forms the Vajra-Constant-Mind.
All devas and the world will feel reverence and affection, giving rise to sympathetic joy; it is able to destroy all internal and external obstacles.
Next is the Vajra-Ḍamaru mudrā: Form the single-pronged shape with the hand of wisdom;
bring it into the palm of the other hand, then open and rotate the fingers of wisdom to raise them up, forming the seal of the Wrathful Vajra-Ḍamaru.
Like an enemy fighting an asura, the heart-mantra is recited while holding the beads in the palms; having empowered them with the mantra,
once the practitioner has finished the recitation, they hold the beads aloft and make great vows.
Binding the samādhi-mudrā, one enters the dharmadhātu-samādhi and cultivates the *svādhiṣṭhāna-dhāraṇī*.
All phenomena are fundamentally unborn, their intrinsic nature transcends verbal expression; they are pure, stainless, and undefiled.
Causes, karma, and so forth are like space; Turning back, one contemplates with discernment, realizing the true reality in every syllable.
Though there are differences between the beginning and the end, that which is realized all returns to the One; One does not abandon this samādhi.
Abiding simultaneously in objectless compassion, may all sentient beings everywhere attain this same stage.
Having recited the root *vidyā* seven times upon emerging from meditative absorption,
one universally makes offerings and offers sublime praise.
For the fire court and the boundary, form the *uṣṇīṣa* mudrā by rotating it counter-clockwise to release [the boundary]; for the invitation, turn it outward.
Reciting *jāla jāla*, one should form the vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*); the two fire-fingers are shaped like lotuses.
From the heart to the face, radiate [light]; at the crown of the head, join the palms in the lotus gesture as before and again protect the body.
Prostrate universally to all the assembly of noble beings, then wander at will as you please.
This concludes the brief explanation of the *homa*.
The Method for Accomplishing Siddhi: Construct a separate hearth facing the maṇḍala;
its shape—square or round—should follow one's specific aim.
Fill the half-hearth with glowing charcoal, and offer ghee, honey, and *guggulu*.
With mustard seeds, sandalwood, frankincense, aloeswood, storax, and resin,
mixed with milk-rice and medicinal incenses, form one hundred and eight pellets;
as the various dharmas are extensively described in the sutras, recite the mantra once for each pellet and cast them into the fire.
The principal deity and the *balis*: may all wishes be fulfilled.
Furthermore, with milk porridge, white mustard seeds, sesame, non-glutinous rice, realgar, and the like, mixed with the sap of the *śvetā* tree and clarified butter.
Casting [offerings] into the hearth brings manifest results;
the ritual for the fire-food of the messengers consists of ghee, honey, milk, and curd,
along with frankincense, white resin, carrots, non-glutinous rice, *kuruṅka* incense, and granulated sugar.
Take rock honey, cypress leaves, and so forth, and pound them together one hundred and eight times.
With each mantra recited, cast one pellet into the furnace as an offering to the messengers,
the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and asuras.
May the retinues of the Four Kings and the Pināyakas joyfully grant their protection; on the eighth or fifteenth day of the month,
always prepare an incense burner and offer various flowers, incense, and food.
Next, paint the image of the Honzon, one chi and five cun in height,
standing in the shape of the letter "T. His feet tread upon blue lotus flowers,
his body is the color of yellow clouds, and his hair is red, curling upward in disarray.
Adorned with various kinds of necklaces and bracelets to embellish the body,
wearing a tiger-skin loincloth, holding a *vajra* in the left hand and extending the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*) with the right, one should assume an extremely swift form.
On the left is painted a Vajra with four arms, yellow in color like clouds,
holding a vajra, a wheel, a noose, and a sword;
the two right arms of the messenger form the fist-mudrā, while the next holds a kapāla.
The waist, arms, and hips are entwined by dragons; in front, he is surrounded by the Kumāra hosts and the eight classes of divine beings.
Above, five-colored auspicious clouds and the various devas scatter exquisite flowers;
[there is] the army of the Trāyastriṃśa Heavenly King.
The four kings each sent their messengers, and the Piṇāyakas all requested their lives and submitted to the teachings.
Regarding the method for painting the images following the ritual of pure fasting for the artist:
the body [of each] shall be five chi and eight cun.
His form is the color of a red lotus; his eyes are two inches long.
His garments are saffron-yellow in color; his feet tread upon golden lotuses.
In his right hand he holds a *vajra*, raised aloft in a threatening gesture.
Holding a golden lotus in his left hand, his hair is slightly yellow and curls to the right;
he wears a single-hair crown that encircles his head. At a height of two inches above the hairline, a transformation Buddha stands within the hair.
He holds a mendicant’s staff in his right hand and a water flask in his left.
On both sides, one faces a Buddha; The golden-hued Sage, holding a *khakkhara* staff, encircles his body.
Amidst dense clouds of five-colored light, when performing the ritual recitation, One should complete the prescribed number of repetitions while facing the image.
As it is taught in the sūtras, for the sake of compassion toward sentient beings,
if one should give rise to wrath, Vajra manifests in an extremely fierce and swift form,
capable of striking terror into those who behold him.
The Yoga Method for the Recitation of the Great Wrathful Vajrakumāra of Pure Body, Speech, and Mind, for Practitioners at All Times. One Fascicle.
